name: Level 2: A2 Struttura
description: Modal verbs (potere, volere, dovere), Passato Prossimo (ha fatto, è andato), and the universal connector 'CHE'.

lessons.title: The Modals: Potere, Volere, Dovere
lessons.subtitle: Can, want, must: How modal verbs govern infinitives in academic statements.
lessons.mentalModel: Modal verbs are followed by an infinitive verb (*può spiegare* = can explain, *deve essere* = must be). In YDS texts, they express possibility, obligation, and hypothesis.

concepts.en: can / is able to / they can

xray.fullEn: This model can explain the phenomenon.

lessons.bridgeMarker: Golden Bridge to Level 4 (YDS): Watch for conditional forms in Level 4: *potrebbe* (could / might) and *dovrebbe* (should / ought to). Recognizing *può* and *deve* now is the key to understanding those!

checkQuiz.question: How do you translate 'The researchers must evaluate the data'?

options.text: I ricercatori devono valutare i dati
I ricercatori possono valutare i dati
I ricercatori vogliono valutare i dati

lessons.title: Passato Prossimo with Avere
lessons.subtitle: The engine for 80% of past actions in Italian (ha detto, hanno confermato).
lessons.mentalModel: Formed with avere + past participle (-ato, -uto, -ito). Notice the subject is singular (ha) or plural (hanno), while the participle ends in -o!
lessons.bridgeMarker: YDS Note: Past participles ending in -to are Latin cognates with English -ted (es. *ha confermato* = has confirmed).

checkQuiz.question: What is the past participle of 'parlare'?

lessons.title: Passato Prossimo with Essere & Agreement
lessons.subtitle: Movement, state verbs, and why the ending agrees with gender/number.
lessons.mentalModel: Verbs of motion and state use essere, and their participle must match gender and number: *è andato* (he went), *è andata* (she went), *sono andati* (they went).
lessons.bridgeMarker: Exam Skill: In YDS biographical reading passages, verbs like *è nato* (was born) and *è vissuto* (lived) appear frequently.

checkQuiz.question: Which sentence is correct for 'The scientist (f) became famous'?
checkQuiz.explanation: With 'essere', the past participle agrees in gender (-a for feminine).

lessons.title: Direct Object Pronouns: Lo, La, Li, Le
lessons.subtitle: Replacing objects to avoid repetition (him, her, it, them).
lessons.mentalModel: These little words sit right in front of the verb: *Lo studio? Lo conosco.* (The study? I know it.)
lessons.bridgeMarker: Reading Tip: Always look back one sentence to see which noun 'lo' or 'la' is pointing to.

checkQuiz.question: In 'I risultati? Li esaminiamo', what does 'Li' refer to?

lessons.title: Indirect Object Pronouns: Gli, Le, Loro
lessons.subtitle: To him, to her, to them: Attribution in academic reporting.
lessons.mentalModel: Used when actions are done to someone: *gli autori gli attribuiscono* (authors attribute to him).

concepts.note: gli dà importanza (gives importance to it/him)

lessons.bridgeMarker: Watch Out: 'Gli' can mean the plural article ('gli scienziati') or the pronoun 'to him'. Check if a verb follows!

checkQuiz.question: What does 'gli' mean when placed immediately before a verb?
checkQuiz.explanation: Before a verb, 'gli' functions as the indirect pronoun 'to him / to it'.

lessons.title: Reflexive Verbs & The Impersonal 'SI'
lessons.subtitle: How 'Si osserva' (it is observed) powers all academic papers.
lessons.mentalModel: Academic papers rarely say 'I think'. They say si ritiene (it is believed) or si osserva (one observes / it is observed). This impersonal 'si' is the king of academic prose!

concepts.en: one observes / it is observed / one notes
it is believed / it is considered

lessons.bridgeMarker: Golden Bridge: 40% of sentences on the YDS use impersonal 'si'! When you see 'si + 3rd person verb', read it as 'it is + [past participle]'.

checkQuiz.question: How do you translate 'Si nota un cambiamento'?

options.text: A change is noted / One notes a change

checkQuiz.explanation: Impersonal 'si' + 3rd person creates the academic passive 'it is noted'.

lessons.title: The Universal Relative Pronoun: CHE
lessons.subtitle: The most frequent connector in Italian: who, whom, which, that.
lessons.mentalModel: CHE connects clauses seamlessly: *il fattore che influenza i risultati* (the factor that influences results). It never changes form!

concepts.note: lo scienziato che studia (the scientist who studies)
i dati che vediamo (the data that we see)

lessons.bridgeMarker: Structure Secret: On YDS sentence completion, 'che' splits the sentence in two. Find the verb inside the 'che' clause first!

checkQuiz.question: What does 'che' translate to when connecting a noun and a verb?
checkQuiz.explanation: 'che' is the invariable relative pronoun meaning that/which/who.

lessons.title: Comparing Things: Più ... di / Meno ... di
lessons.subtitle: More than, less than, as ... as: Comparing research outcomes.
lessons.mentalModel: Used to compare two entities: *più grande di* (bigger than), *meno efficace di* (less effective than), *tanto ... quanto* (as ... as).
lessons.bridgeMarker: YDS Trap: 'Di' is used before nouns (*più di Roma*), but 'che' is used before adjectives or verbs (*più interessante che utile*).

checkQuiz.question: How do you say 'more efficient than'?

lessons.title: Adverbs of Frequency & Manner (-mente)
lessons.subtitle: Chiaramente, recentemente, principalmente: Modifying claims.
lessons.mentalModel: Just like '-ly' in English, Italian adds -mente to the feminine adjective: *chiara* -> *chiaramente* (clearly), *recente* -> *recentemente* (recently).
lessons.bridgeMarker: Cognate Power: 90% of -mente adverbs are transparent English cognates (generalmente = generally, naturalmente = naturally).

checkQuiz.question: What is the English meaning of 'recentemente'?

lessons.title: Time Horizons & Duration: Da, Fa, Durante, Prima, Dopo
lessons.subtitle: Tracking chronology in historical and scientific passages.
lessons.mentalModel: Time markers define the timeline: *da tre anni* (for three years / since), *tre anni fa* (three years ago), *prima di* (before), *dopo* (after).

concepts.note: Lavora qui da tre anni (has worked here for 3 years)

lessons.bridgeMarker: ÖSYM Test Question: 'Da' with a present tense verb translates to English Present Perfect ('has been doing'). Crucial for translation questions!

checkQuiz.question: How do you translate 'five years ago'?
checkQuiz.explanation: 'fa' placed after the time unit means 'ago'.

lessons.title: Future Tense Reading Markers (-rà, -ranno)
lessons.subtitle: Recognizing predictions, forecasts, and hypotheses.
lessons.mentalModel: The future tense is characterized by the stressed endings -rà (singular: *sarà*, *farà*, *mostrerà*) and -ranno (plural: *saranno*, *faranno*, *mostreranno*).
lessons.bridgeMarker: Future vs Conditional: Don't confuse -rà (future: will) with -rebbe (conditional: would)! Future has one 'r', conditional has double 'rr'.

checkQuiz.question: What does 'La ricerca mostrerà nuovi dati' mean?

options.text: The research will show new data

checkQuiz.explanation: 'mostrerà' is the future tense ending in -rà (will show).
